messages:
maya: quick share — ran microbench for two fused-QKV packing strategies ("stride" vs "cascade") plus a bias+rope epilogue fuse. short-seq wins look promising (8-12%); long-seq + paged-KV shows regression. pasted numbers below.

sam: nice, can you drop the bench table and the exact command you ran?

maya: sure — trimmed output here:

```
# bench summary (tokens/s)  | seq128 | seq512 | seq2048
baseline-unpacked           | 12000  | 8200   | 3400
stride-packed + epilogue    | 13400  | 9100   | 3000  # +11% / +10% / -11.7%
cascade-packed + epilogue  | 13100  | 9000   | 3050  # +9% / +9.7% / -10.3%

env: continuous_batch=true, max_batch_size=32, max_latency_ms=12
paged_kv: enabled, page_size=64k
GPU: A100-40GB, driver: 525.xx, cuda: 12.1
```

leo: that seq2048 regression with paged_kv is worrying. what's the kvcache hit rate and swap stats? also, did you run with our new batching heuristic (latency-first)?

maya: hit-rate for paged kv was ~0.72 at seq512 but dropped to 0.41 at seq2048 (working set >> page_size). swap count spiked and L2 miss% went way up. we used the latency-first batcher (recent PR) — it increases batch packing density which amplifies register pressure in the fused epilogue.

brynn: could be register spill + more scatter loads from paged pages. cascade packing reduces some writes but still keeps more live regs in the epilogue. did you check spill stores in nvprof/nsys?

perf-bot: perf-alert: nightly/regressions — job fused-qkv-cascade detected -5.8% regression vs baseline on seq2048 (threshold 3%). See run 2024-11-09-03.

maya: yep — nvprof shows increased local memory stores around the epilogue kernel (spill). pprof flame also shows the epilogue takes ~22% of time for seq2048 vs ~9% for seq512. suspicion: epilogue fusion (bias+rope+gelu) pushes register usage beyond the optimal point on Ampere, causing spill and L2 thrash that paged-KV magnifies.

sam: proposed mitigations:
1) heuristic: disable full epilogue fusion for seq_len > 1024 or when paged_kv=true
2) implement split-epilogue: do bias+rope in a small fused path and defer activation/gating to a lightweight second kernel (keeps hot regs small)
3) fallback to unpacked qkv kernel for very large batches or high kvcache-paged ratios

leo: also: extend kernel-chooser signals to include `kvcache_paged_ratio` and `epilogue_reg_pressure` (derived from kernel compile-time reg usage). prefer low-reg kernels when paged ratio > 0.5.

brynn: I'll prototype split-epilogue (bias+rope fused, activation separate) — rough timeline: POC this week, bench next. can someone share the exact nvprof command and the pprof flame link?

maya: uploaded traces and flame to internal gist: https://internal.gist/trace-1749001234 (nvprof, nsys, pprof svg). nvprof command I ran: `nvprof --metrics l2_hit_rate,dram_utilization,sm_efficiency -- ./bench_fused_attn --seq 2048 --batch 8 --paged-kv`

sam: SG. I'll add a bench sweep for page_size {32k,64k,128k}, seq {256,512,1024,2048}, batcher {latency-first, throughput-first} to the nightly matrix. will also add a flag to toggle epilogue fusion to collect controlled numbers.

maya: assignment summary: brynn -> split-epilogue POC; sam -> bench matrix + nightly; leo -> kernel-chooser heuristic and metric; maya -> repro + upload logs + coordination. will follow up Wednesday in sync.

leo: one more thought — on Hopper or newer, register file is larger; we should annotate kernels with an arch-preference and let chooser prefer epilogue-fused on Hopper but not Ampere.

brynn: noted. will keep POC arch-agnostic but measure Ampere vs Hopper.

sam: adding TODO: update perf tests to capture kvcache miss counters and epilogue spill stores in bench reports so chooser can learn from historical runs.

maya: thanks all. quick reaction thread end: brynn: :thumbsup:  leo: :thumbsup:  sam: :thumbsup:
